decisions.decision: The Preview environment for V2-022 is the `preview-local` grade of docs/architecture/release-contract.md section 3, and the exercise is one live Go test process: `internal/api/live_dogfood_test.go`, package `api_test`, one top-level `TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood` with ordered subtests, gated on `AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_DOGFOOD=1` (plus `AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_PROVIDER=1` for the subtests that invoke the real claude CLI). It builds `cmd/control-plane` from the source tree and runs it as a real OS process on 127.0.0.1 against a real Firestore emulator started by `scripts/firestore-emulator.sh`, exactly as V2-051's `internal/api/live_local_test.go` already does, drives every owner-facing capability over real HTTP, drives the runner-facing protocol over real HTTP as an enrolled Runner session, and spawns the real `claude` CLI as a real child process group through `runner.SupervisedInvocationRunner` with a `runner.CostLedger`.
decisions.rationale: Every mechanism this needs already exists and is exported: `runner.ProcessSupervisor`, `runner.SupervisedInvocationRunner`, `runner.CostLedger`, `runner.LoadPreflightRecord`, `provider.ClaudeAdapter`, `update.Install`/`update.Switch`, `release.AssembleCandidate`/`Pipeline.Promote`, and the whole `/v1` surface. Putting the exercise in `internal/api` reuses V2-051's proven composition (build + real process + real emulator + real HTTP) instead of inventing a second one, and avoids creating a new component: `test/` does not exist and `ci/components.json` (prohibited) would have to be edited to own it, which would invalidate all 23 component evidence keys.

decisions.decision: An evidence id may be written into `contracts/release-contract/foundation.json` for a capability if and only if BOTH hold, measured, not argued: (1) the capability's declared `outcome_conditions.success` sentence in `contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json` was observed in full during the live run, and (2) every system in that capability's declared `external_dependencies.systems` and `.providers` was actually connected to. Applying this rule to the twelve declarations yields exactly three eligible capabilities: `cap-requirement-intake`, `cap-backlog-visibility`, `cap-user-documentation`. The other nine are ineligible for a named, recorded reason (d3), and their `evidence_ids` stay `[]`.
decisions.rationale: release-contract.md section 3 says external-system-dependent capabilities must connect to the real system, and gate rule G3-1 refuses local substitution for a named external resource. Four capabilities (`cap-preview-operation`, `cap-stable-promotion`, `cap-loop-control`, `cap-loop-self-update`) declare `Google Cloud Run`, so their evidence belongs to D1 by declaration, not by convenience. Two (`cap-repository-registration`, `cap-autonomous-resolution`) declare `GitHub`, and this repository contains no GitHub client at all (a full-tree grep for go-github, api.github.com and GITHUB_TOKEN finds only prose inside .agents/ records). Three more declare all three Providers (M6/V2-028) and have no implemented observation surface. Deriving eligibility from the declaration text makes the answer falsifiable and reproducible instead of a judgement call.

decisions.decision: Every ineligible capability is attributed to exactly one of three buckets, and the bucket is recorded in the evidence record and in `docs/preview/stable-diff.md`. Bucket D1 (deferred to the initial deploy gate, V2-054, conditions (ii) scale-to-zero and (iv) deploy path): `cap-preview-operation`, `cap-stable-promotion`, `cap-loop-control`, `cap-loop-self-update`. Bucket MILESTONE (owned by a later milestone that is already planned): `cap-autonomous-resolution` and `cap-provider-operation` and `cap-shared-resource-allocation` for their three-Provider half (M6/V2-028) and `cap-shared-resource-allocation` for its multi-Repository half (M7/V2-030, V2-031). Bucket ESCALATION (no owner today; the capability's observable result has no implementation, so it is not an environment problem and D1 would never fix it): E22-1 Repository registration, Git and GitHub are absent entirely; E22-2 the needs-input question surface is absent; E22-3 `internal/release` is imported by nothing outside itself, so there is no owner-visible Preview version, promotion-condition or rollback display (this is V2-021's already-recorded escalation E2); E22-4 there is no Provider registry, health, limit or assignment surface; E22-5 `internal/scheduler` is imported by nothing outside itself and no control mode sets a concurrency limit.
decisions.rationale: The M5 completion condition and the task's non_goals both turn on not treating an unexecutable capability as promotable. Saying only 'not exercisable' would let a reader assume D1 will fix it. Five of the nine will not be fixed by any deploy: they have no code. Separating 'wrong environment' from 'no implementation' from 'later milestone' is the difference between a roadmap and an excuse, and it tells Sol precisely which new Requirements M5's closure actually needs.

decisions.decision: Writing evidence ids requires first moving the release off the unexercised baseline. `internal/contracts.TestFoundationReleaseContractBaseline` treats any `release` whose prerelease identifier is exactly `baseline` as the unexercised baseline and then requires every capability's `evidence_ids` to be empty; the same test's clauses (e) and (f) require every non-empty evidence id to resolve in `.agents/v2/evidence/index.json` and require `documentation.stable` for any capability claiming `status: stable`. So V2-022 renames the release from `0.1.0-baseline` to `0.1.0-preview.1` in `contracts/release-contract/foundation.json` (`id` becomes `rc-foundation-0.1.0-preview.1`) and in `contracts/release-contract/foundation-capabilities.json` (`id`, `release`, `contract_ref`), updates the `Release:` marker in `docs/preview/index.md`, and un-pins the two literal `0.1.0-baseline` assertions in `internal/release/baseline_test.go` and `internal/release/contract_baseline_test.go`. No capability's `status` changes: all twelve stay `preview`, and `docs/stable/index.md` keeps the exact marker `Stable release: none`.
decisions.rationale: The baseline marker is a machine-enforced statement that the release has never been exercised. After this repository has been exercised as a Preview target that statement is false, and it is also the only thing that makes a non-empty `evidence_ids` impossible. The rename is therefore not incidental: it is the mechanism. Renaming while leaving all statuses at `preview` keeps the anti-fabrication invariants (e) and (f) live and keeps `docs/stable/index.md` truthful, because no Stable release is being claimed.

decisions.decision: Two commits, in this order. Commit A: the live test file, the new `internal/contracts/capability_evidence_test.go`, the two un-pinned `internal/release` test literals, the release rename with `evidence_ids` still `[]`, and every documentation change. `devbox run --pure -- make check` must be green at commit A. Commit B: `contracts/release-contract/foundation.json`'s `evidence_ids` for the eligible capabilities, the two evidence records, and their two `index.json` entries, together, and `make check` must be green again on the committed state. The composite `evidence_key` of both records is read with `devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys` at commit A's green tree over the eleven constituent components commit B does not move.
decisions.rationale: Clause (f) requires an evidence id to resolve in the index, so `foundation.json`'s ids and the index entries that satisfy them must land in the same commit; splitting them makes `make check` red in between. Commit B touches `contracts/**` and `.agents/**`, which moves the `contracts`, `internal-contracts`, `release` and `task-ledger` keys, so those four must not appear in the composite key or the record would stale itself the moment it is committed. `gitleaks git` only scans committed history, so the second `make check` after commit B is the only one that proves the record's own 64-hex digests passed the secret gate.

decisions.decision: The composite `evidence_key` for both V2-022 evidence records is `sha256` of the literal ASCII string `api=<key>;application=<key>;control-plane=<key>;docs=<key>;domain=<key>;infra=<key>;provider=<key>;runner=<key>;store-firestore=<key>;update=<key>;web=<key>` with the component ids in that fixed order and each `<key>` exactly as `make evidence-keys` reported it at commit A. The record states this method verbatim in a check summary.
decisions.rationale: `release-live-dogfood` and `provider-live-claude-dogfood` are synthesised live-exercise component names that do not exist in `ci/components.json`, so they have no per-component key. Gate rule G6 accepts a composite key only when the record declares how it was computed, and V2-051/V2-060 already established the semicolon-joined `id=<key>` convention; reusing it keeps one method in the repository instead of two. The eleven constituents are exactly the components whose bytes the live exercise executes, and none of their closures contain `contracts/**` or `.agents/**`.

decisions.decision: Two evidence records, not one. `.agents/v2/evidence/V2-022-release-live-dogfood.json` (`ev-v2-022-release-live-dogfood`, component `release-live-dogfood`) carries the capability exercise matrix, the channel break/resume journey, and the promotability verification. `.agents/v2/evidence/V2-022-provider-live-claude-dogfood.json` (`ev-v2-022-provider-live-claude-dogfood`, component `provider-live-claude-dogfood`) carries everything the real claude CLI touched, including the ledger snapshot, and carries an `artifact_refs` entry with `artifact_id` `provider-preflight` whose sha256 equals the V2-022 preflight record file, with `observed_at` strictly later than the record's `approval.approved_at`.
decisions.rationale: `internal/contracts.CheckProviderPreflightLedger` applies its strict anti-fabrication cross-check to exactly those evidence entries whose component begins with `provider-live-`: one matching preflight record per task_id, an artifact_ref digest that matches the record's bytes, and approval strictly preceding observation. Naming the provider half `provider-live-claude-dogfood` opts this task's real-CLI usage into that existing machine check instead of leaving it unchecked under a component name the checker ignores. It also keeps the two environment classes legible to G3, which distinguishes grades by component name.

decisions.decision: A new deterministic test, `internal/contracts/capability_evidence_test.go`, makes the link between a claimed capability evidence id and a real passed exercise machine-checked and bidirectional. For every capability in `foundation.json` with a non-empty `evidence_ids`, every referenced record must contain a `checks` entry whose `name` is exactly the capability id and whose `status` is `passed`. Conversely, for every check in a V2-022 evidence record whose `name` equals one of the twelve capability ids and whose `status` is `passed`, that capability's `evidence_ids` must reference that record. The test is a new file; no existing test file is edited.
decisions.rationale: Clause (f) only proves an evidence id resolves to some record; it does not prove the record says anything about that capability. Keying the claim to a per-check name lets a record be honestly `partial` overall (nine capabilities were not exercised) while still proving the three specific claims it does make. The converse direction is the more valuable half: it makes it impossible to quietly exercise a capability successfully and then omit it, which is the failure mode that would let a later release under-report what it had proved.

decisions.decision: Breaking the Preview is done at the Loop channel layer with `internal/update`, on two real builds of `cmd/control-plane`. The good build comes from the repository tree; the broken build comes from a copy of the tree in `t.TempDir()` with one deliberate, described defect applied to the copy only (for example the capture handler returning 500), so no tracked file changes. Both are installed as real signed bundles through `update.Install` with an ephemeral test-generated ed25519 keypair, `update.Switch(root, "stable", good)` and `update.Switch(root, "preview", broken)` set the channel symlinks, and the process actually served on 127.0.0.1 is the one the channel symlink resolves to. The journey is: capture a Requirement while the stable channel serves; switch the preview channel in and serve the broken build; observe the failure over real HTTP and observe that a Runner claim against the broken Preview fails; roll the channel back to the previously verified stable version; observe that the same Requirement, from the same Firestore emulator canonical state, is still there and advances to a terminal state under the restored build.
decisions.rationale: This is the only Preview/Stable routing that exists as running code: `internal/release`'s `Router` is a library nothing imports, and Repository-level Preview routing has no API surface (escalation E22-3). `update.Switch` is atomic, refuses an uninstalled version, and deliberately does not delete the prior target, so rollback is the same operation with the prior verified version. Using it also lets the exercise observe, live, the separation V2-021 recorded in prose: channel rollback and release-route rollback are different layers, and `internal/release` deliberately does not import `internal/update`.

decisions.decision: No first Stable promotion is attempted, and the absence of a previous Stable release is not worked around. The Requirement-resume half of the M5 completion condition is satisfied against the previously verified Loop channel version from d9, at the self-host grade release-contract.md section 3 already anticipates while D1 is unpassed. `docs/stable/index.md` keeps `Stable release: none`, no capability status becomes `stable`, and the evidence record states in plain words that the resumed-on-previous-Stable claim is a Loop channel claim and not a Release Contract Stable release.
decisions.rationale: Promoting would require capability evidence for all twelve capabilities; nine cannot be exercised (d2, d3), five of them because the code does not exist. Manufacturing that evidence is precisely the task's first non_goal, and the machine already refuses it three ways: `CompileContract` rejects `status: stable` with empty `evidence_ids`, clause (e) additionally demands a `documentation.stable` anchor that no capability declaration has, and `domain.ReleaseCandidate.CanPromote` demands per-capability `CapabilityEvidence` bound to the candidate's own digests. Asking whether the first Stable promotion should come first has a clean answer: it cannot come first, because promotion is downstream of the very evidence this task is trying to produce.

decisions.decision: The promotability verification is two-sided and both sides run in the same live process, so the digests are the ones actually observed. Negative side, on the real repository tree: `release.AssembleCandidate(root, ...)` with no fabricated evidence must still refuse, and the refusal must name a capability whose `evidence_ids` is empty; the measured set of capabilities the gate refuses for must equal the nine ineligible ids of d3 exactly, at commit B. Positive side, hermetic: in a synthetic tree under `t.TempDir()` whose contract declares only the eligible capabilities, build `domain.CapabilityEvidence` for each from that assembly's own `CandidateDigest`, `BundleDigest`, `ContractDigest` and `DocsDigest` with `Target` `preview-local` and `Provider` `claude`, set `RollbackEvidence` and `ResumeEvidence` from the d9 journey's actual outcome, and assert `CanPromote() == nil` and that `Pipeline.Promote` reaches `domain.ReleaseStable`. Then flip one byte of one documentation member of that synthetic tree and assert the same candidate is refused.
decisions.rationale: 'Filling evidence_ids makes the candidate promotable' is false for the Foundation candidate and true for the mechanism, and stating only one of those is dishonest. The negative side turns 'not promotable' from a blanket fact into a measurement whose refusal set is checkable against d3, so a future release can watch that set shrink. The positive side proves the gate is not permanently jammed, using digests and booleans that came from the real run rather than from constants, and the docs-drift flip keeps the positive control from silently degenerating into a test that passes for any candidate.

decisions.decision: The real claude CLI runs under a V2-022-specific provider-preflight record, `.agents/v2/provider-preflight/V2-022-provider-live-claude-dogfood.json`, with `task_id` `V2-022`, its own ledger at `/home/takushi/.local/state/agentic-loop/v2/V2-022-provider-cost.json`, `max_invocations` 24, `max_total_cost_usd` 20.00, `worst_case_reservation_usd` 1.00, `environment.granted_names` empty, and `approval.subject_path` `.agents/v2/packets/provider-standing-authorization.json` with `subject_digest` equal to that file's sha256. The planned accounted usage is eight invocations: one for the autonomous-resolution journey, one for the graceful-stop-against-a-live-child journey, one for the Provider connection journey, and one for the resumed Requirement after the channel rollback, each run twice for the stability probe of d14. The single-invocation anomaly threshold stays the code constant `runner.CostAnomalyThresholdUSD` (2.00 USD) and is not configurable.
decisions.rationale: V2-017's ledger is bound to V2-017's work order digest and already holds eleven of sixteen entries; reusing it would either fail `LoadPreflightRecord` or exhaust mid-run, and editing it would destroy the evidence trail. Binding the new record's approval to the standing authorization packet rather than to this work order is what the preflight schema's own description asks for, and it means a later edit to the work order cannot silently invalidate the record. Twenty-four against eight planned is a three-times headroom: large enough for named retries (V2-017 spent three invocations on one journey fixing real bugs) and small enough that a runaway loop trips it long before it becomes a subscription anomaly. Measured mean cost per invocation in V2-017 was about 0.074 USD, so 20.00 USD is roughly a 30x margin over the expected total and functions purely as a runaway detector.

decisions.decision: Reaching any preflight threshold is a stop for inspection and is recorded as such: neither a success nor a capability failure. If the ledger halts or refuses, the affected capability's check is recorded with `status` `failed` and a summary naming the refusal reason, no evidence id is written for it, the record's `result` stays `partial`, and the task stops. The record's `limits` must not be edited, the ledger file must not be edited or reinitialised, and `halted` must not be cleared; the only remedy is a new owner-issued preflight record, possibly with a new ledger path.
decisions.rationale: The owner's standing authorization removes the count and money ceiling as an approval question, which makes the thresholds pure anomaly detectors. An anomaly detector that the detected party is allowed to raise detects nothing, and clearing `halted` erases the only record of what tripped it. This is already documented for V2-017 in docs/operations/provider-live-claude.md; restating it in the work order keeps the rule attached to the task that will be tempted by it.

decisions.decision: Flaky handling is a stability probe, not a retry. The entire live argv is executed twice as two separate processes, each with `-count=1`, on the same commit and therefore the same candidate digests. A capability's check may be recorded `passed` only if both runs observed it passing. If the two runs disagree for any sub-exercise, that sub-exercise's check is recorded `failed` with both observations transcribed and the disagreement named, no evidence id is written for the affected capability, the record's `result` is `partial`, and the task stops and escalates. The first failure is never deleted, no third run is used to break the tie, and quarantine is not available without a target, a deadline, a responsible Requirement and alternative coverage.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 9 forbids promoting a result that varied on the same candidate and says a Preview live exercise's flakiness stops promotion outright, and the task's second non_goal names overwriting flaky evidence with a retry. A third run would be exactly that overwrite dressed as diligence. Two runs also cost twice the provider usage, which is why d12 budgets for it rather than discovering it mid-run.

decisions.decision: The live gate skips by default and fails loudly when misconfigured. With `AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_DOGFOOD` unset the test calls `t.Logf` naming the unmet condition and `t.Skip`, so `devbox run --pure -- make check` performs zero provider invocations and starts zero processes. With the gate set but `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` unset, or the V2-022 preflight record missing or schema-invalid, or its ledger path unwritable, the test calls `t.Fatal`, never `t.Skip`. The evidence must record the skip count of the live runs as zero and must record the ledger entry count immediately before and immediately after a `make check` run to prove that number is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Gate rule G7 refuses to count a skipped test as a pass, and a live suite that silently skips is the single easiest way to fabricate a green Preview exercise. V2-051 and V2-017 both established the Skip-by-default plus Fatal-when-half-configured pattern, and V2-017's before/after ledger count measurement is the concrete proof that the default path really costs nothing.

decisions.decision: Every capability check in the evidence records must carry the section 3 environment identifiers: environment class `preview-local`; machine identifier from `hostname` and `uname -sr`; emulator name, version and project (`firebase --version`, `agentic-loop-test`) and the emulator host and port actually used; the claude CLI's absolute path and `--version` output; the Go toolchain version; and, for every real invocation, the CLI-issued `session_id`. Prompts and raw responses are never recorded, in any form, in any file.
decisions.rationale: Section 3's last bullet makes those identifiers a requirement of the evidence, not a nicety, and G3-2 repeats it for exactly this grade: a `preview-local` record without the machine, the emulator and the external system identifiers cannot be distinguished from a unit test afterwards. Section 7 permits provider-issued execution identifiers and forbids prompts and raw output, and V2-048 already put that permission in writing, so `session_id` is the strongest identifier available and the ceiling at the same time.

decisions.decision: Rollback for the whole task is a git revert of its two commits plus three out-of-repository cleanups, and all of them are enumerated up front: the V2-022 cost ledger at `/home/takushi/.local/state/agentic-loop/v2/V2-022-provider-cost.json` is left in place as the evidence trail and never edited or deleted; the Firestore emulator data is ephemeral and dies with the script-managed emulator process; every channel root, installed version and workspace lives under `t.TempDir()`. No GCP resource, no GitHub object, no notification and no public exposure is created, and the only network destination reached is the claude CLI's own endpoint via the CLI itself.
decisions.rationale: The task's third non_goal forbids cost, notification or public exposure outside declared test resources, and the only way to keep that checkable is to declare the full side-effect surface before the run rather than to assert afterwards that there was none. Keeping the ledger is the one deliberate exception: it is the record of what the run consumed, so deleting it during rollback would destroy exactly the evidence the guard exists to produce.

decisions.decision: The recorded escalations are E22-1 through E22-10 and none of them may be decided by the implementer: E22-1 no Repository registration route, no Repository aggregate registration command, and no Git or GitHub client anywhere in the tree; E22-2 no needs-input question surface (the domain status and command exist, the application command, the API route and the detail fields do not); E22-3 `internal/release` is imported by nothing outside itself, so no Preview version, promotion-condition or rollback state is observable (V2-021's E2); E22-4 no Provider registry, health, limit or assignment surface; E22-5 `internal/scheduler` is imported by nothing outside itself and no control mode sets a concurrency limit; E22-6 `cmd/runner` refuses to run without `--fake` and states it has no control-plane wiring, so the shipped Runner binary cannot claim from a live Control Plane; E22-7 `GET /v1/requirements` accepts only `page_size` and `cursor`, so the Backlog cannot be filtered by Repository; E22-8 `ControlReadModel` carries no target Runner, process, lease or side-effect-permitted projection; E22-9 the live exercise file's imports exceed the `api` component's declared dependency edges, so selective CI would not select it on a change to `internal/runner`, `internal/update` or `internal/release` (the sibling of V2-021's E1, and `ci/components.json` is prohibited); E22-10 the owner console serves no document route, so at `preview-local` the owner reads the repository working tree.
decisions.rationale: Five of these are the reason nine capabilities cannot be exercised, so leaving them as prose in a report would lose the only mechanically derived list of what M5's closure is actually missing. Naming E22-6 and E22-9 matters even though neither blocks the exercise: they bound what the evidence is allowed to claim, so a later reader cannot read 'the Runner claimed and drove a real Provider' as 'the Runner daemon works'. Each is a boundary question about ownership and scope, which is Sol's to answer, not something to resolve inside an implementation attempt with a retry budget of two.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_DOGFOOD=1 -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_PROVIDER=1 -e HOME=/home/takushi -e PATH=<devbox-pure-PATH>:/home/takushi/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -timeout 3600s -run TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood ./internal/api
risks: Nine of twelve capabilities are ineligible for an evidence id, five of them because their observable result has no implementation at all. The honest outcome of this task is a partial record and a candidate that is still not promotable, and the value delivered is that the refusal set is now measured and named rather than blanket.

Renaming the release off the baseline moves the contracts, internal-contracts, release and task-ledger component keys, which stales ev-v2-021-release and ev-v2-009-release-contract. Re-issuing those is make evidence-all work owned by the M5 gate (V2-026), not by this task, but the M5 gate must be told.

The stability probe doubles real provider usage. If the second run disagrees with the first for any sub-exercise, the affected capability produces no evidence id and the task stops; that is the designed outcome, not a failure to plan around.

The live exercise file's imports exceed the api component's declared dependency edges (E22-9). Selective CI will not re-run it when internal/runner, internal/update or internal/release change, so the exercise is a durable Preview workflow, not a per-commit gate.

The broken Preview build is produced by editing a copy of the tree in t.TempDir(). If the defect is applied to the tracked tree by mistake, make check at commit A catches it, but the run must be redone; the defect must be described in the evidence as a path plus a one-line description, never committed.

cmd/runner cannot claim from a live Control Plane (E22-6), so the runner-side protocol is driven by the live test process over real HTTP. The exercise is real, but no claim about the shipped Runner daemon may be made from it.
